title: Messages between AI agents, as the Identity Agent that holds them records them (ADR-047)
description: Every message is signed twice. The sender signs a statement (a body, with its machine key) or a request (a person, from a paired controller). The Identity Agent then countersigns a record of it, as the AI agent the message is from, in a signed DIDComm envelope whose body is the record. Worked examples, with signatures, are in identity-agent-core/agentmessage/message-vectors.json.

statement_bytes.description: What a body signs: the lines IA-AGENT-MSG-V1, conversation, kind, from, to, in_reply_to, body_hash, brain.provider, brain.model, brain.session, brain.run_hash, host, host_nonce, host_time, body_credential, joined with a newline (0x0a), no trailing newline. An absent field is an empty line. The signature is made with the body's machine key and encoded as for a signed request (see contracts/agent-body).

statement.description: A body's statement. Refused unless every required field is non-empty, no field holds a carriage return or newline, kind is one of the four, in_reply_to is present (a body only ever speaks about a message it was given, so even an ask names the message it was handling), host_nonce is at least 16 characters and host_time is RFC 3339.

in_reply_to.description: the message this one acts on; required by the check although the field may be left out of the JSON

body_credential.description: the AI Agent Body credential that made host this AI agent's body

brain.description: What produced the words, as the body reports it. The body's word, not the model provider's.

run_hash.description: a digest of everything the brain was sent and returned in the run

party.description: An AI agent's identifier, or person: followed by a person's identifier.

digest.description: Blake3-256 of the words, CESR qb64 with code E.

person_message.description: What a person's controller signs to say something to an AI agent: the words themselves, so the signature covers them.

conversation.description: absent to open a new conversation

controller_proof.description: A person's own statement: the request their controller signed, kept as the exact string signed. Its second line is the controller and its last line the Blake3-256 (CESR) of request.

public_key.description: the controller's key, as its Controller Grant records it

controller_grant.description: the controller's Controller Grant credential, when it has one

person_ref.description: The person a controller acts for, as the Identity Agent established it.

record.description: One entry in a conversation, as the Identity Agent countersigns it. It carries exactly one sender's proof: statement with host_signature and host_verkey, or controller_proof. What the record says must be what the sender signed. prev_hash is the hash of the entry before it in the conversation (see entry_hash), empty for the first.

depth.description: how far down a chain of asks: a person's message is 0

body_grade.description: the grade of the body it came from, stamped by the Identity Agent

jwm.description: The countersigned message: id is the record's message_id, type is agent-message, from is did:keri: and the countersigner, to is did:keri: and the recipient (a person's identifier without person:), created_time is the record's ia_time and body is the record.

envelope.description: A signed DIDComm envelope (mode signed). plaintext is the base64url (no padding) of the JWM's JSON. ed_sig and mldsa_sig are base64url Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 signatures by the countersigner's messaging keys over those JSON bytes followed directly by E and the base64url (no padding) of the Blake3-256 of the JWM's body bytes. Both must verify. The countersigner is the AI agent the message is from, or the Identity Agent itself for a person's message.

entry_hash.description: An entry's place in its conversation's chain: Blake3-256 (CESR qb64, code E) of plaintext, a newline, ed_sig, a newline, mldsa_sig, all as they appear in the envelope.

messaging_keys.description: A countersigner's public messaging keys, base64url. kel_sig, when present, is a signature by the identifier's current key over these keys.
